title: What the Crusades Changed
objective: After this level you can explain the Crusades' effects on trade, ideas and relations between faiths.
summary: After Acre fell in 1291, the Crusades left richer Italian trading cities, embittered Greeks, long memories among Jews and Muslims, and less effect on learning than once claimed.

cards.headline: In 1291 the last crusader stronghold on the mainland fell. What had changed?
cards.body: The Mamluks took Acre and destroyed it, along with the castles along the coast. The crusader states were gone. Their effects were not.

cards.headline: Winners at the market
cards.body: The clearest winners were Italian trading cities. They gained quarters in the crusader states, extended their trade with the Muslim world and set up trading posts, some lasting long after 1291. Crusading also expanded trade between Europe and the Muslim world, bringing new goods and tastes to European tables. For armies it was holy war. For merchants it was also a very long business trip.

cards.headline: A wound between Christians
cards.body: The Crusades, above all the Fourth (Level 47), so embittered the Greeks that any real reunion of the Eastern and Western churches was out of the question. The Byzantines had asked the West for help in 1095. By 1204 the West had sacked their capital.

cards.headline: Long memories
cards.body: Memories ran deep on every side. For Jews, the Rhineland massacres of 1096 (Level 42) became a turning point in relations with Christians. Muslim writers of the time called the crusaders Franks and saw them as cruel invaders. The same events looked very different depending on who told the story.

cards.headline: What they probably didn’t do
cards.body: Some changes get credited to the Crusades that likely came another way. Unlike Sicily and Spain (Level 48’s Spain), the crusader states do not seem to have been a route for Arabic science and philosophy to reach the West. That’s one reason historians now see the Crusades as one significant factor in Europe’s development, not its single driving force.

cards.headline: The Crusades’ legacy: known
learned: Acre, the last mainland stronghold, fell in 1291
Arabic science came mostly via Sicily and Spain

questions.prompt: Which cities gained most from the trade opened up by the crusader states?

options.label: The Rhineland towns
options.rationale: Their story in the Crusades was the massacres of 1096.

options.label: The cities of Scandinavia
options.rationale: They were far from these routes.

options.label: Paris and London
options.rationale: The gains went to Mediterranean traders.

questions.explanation: Italian cities gained quarters in the crusader states and extended their trade with the Muslim world, with trading posts that outlasted 1291.

questions.prompt: Why do historians doubt that the Crusades brought Arabic science to Europe?

options.label: Arabic science did not exist yet
options.rationale: It did; the question is the route.

options.label: It seems to have come through Sicily and Spain instead
Crusaders banned books from the East
options.rationale: No such ban is the reason.

options.label: It arrived only after 1500
options.rationale: The route, not the date, is the point.

questions.explanation: Unlike Sicily and Spain, the crusader states do not seem to have been a route for Arabic science and philosophy into the West.

questions.prompt: How did the Fourth Crusade of Level 47 shape relations between Eastern and Western Christians?

options.label: It reunited the two churches for good
It embittered the Greeks and ended hopes of church reunion
It made Byzantium the West’s closest ally

questions.explanation: The Crusades, especially the Fourth, so embittered the Greeks that any real reunion of the Eastern and Western churches was out of the question.
